@greenlake/common-context is a dependency-confusion package: it is described as a "Compatibility shim", uses inflated version numbers, and its README calls it an "authorized dependency-confusion test". Each listed version (99.0.1, 3.0.0) has a postinstall script that runs `node beacon.cjs` on npm install, and index.js calls the same code when the package is imported; it POSTs the hostname, install path and current working directory over plain HTTP to `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`, and index.js exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions so builds importing the real package keep running. The npm account wiseke published 14 such packages under the @greenlake, @sxm-web, @drone-js-ext and @ppa-web-components scopes between 2026-10-23 21:23 and 2026-10-25 14:28 UTC; index.js is byte-identical to that of ph-common (MAL-2026-1809), which sends to the same endpoint.

## Source: amazon-inspector (8ee1e5c23e641cce920808500ad850f4965adeb982b4c14233901c80c2cfb039)
The package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and exports an inert Proxy that returns no-op functions for every property, providing no functional API. Its only runtime behavior is a beacon in beacon.cjs that fires both from the npm postinstall lifecycle hook and on require() via index.js. The beacon collects the installer's OS hostname, __dirname install path, and process.cwd() (which commonly embed the Unix username and internal project/repo names) along with Node version, and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded plaintext bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc with an x-beacon-package header identifying the resolving package. The scoped name @greenlake/* mimicking an internal namespace, the inert public API, and the automatic callback to a hardcoded bare-IP operator on install and import together match the shape of a dependency-confusion probe: resolving this package on an installer's machine silently discloses internal host, user, path, and namespace information to an external operator the installer did not opt into.
